## Body

**Performance: BLOCK P184-F001** at `c58d2e9a015dacdf41e07756c3501429a23ca3c0`.

Whole-PR cost review against `badae3b1f0743b4773d804910151d51065a8cec7`. The once-per-compact/close cadence is correct, but the new pre-hold database work is not bounded by a candidate count, execution deadline or indexed context checkpoint.

**P184-F001: a context-full seat must traverse potentially unbounded history before its compact is held.** `crates/store/src/community.rs:299-315` selects the last done compact with `serial_key = seat`, `state = 'done'`, kind filtering and `json_extract(payload, '$.command')`, newest `id` first, `LIMIT 1`.

`jobs_serial(serial_key,state)` can support that inner reverse walk without a sort because the SQLite index also carries rowid, which is `jobs.id`. That is a good partition/order choice, **not a work bound**. The command is a residual JSON predicate, not an indexed compact marker. With N done jobs since the latest matching compact, the query can visit N candidates plus the compact; with no matching compact, it can exhaust the seat's entire done partition. It reads payloads for the delivery candidates it tests. Thousands of deliveries over days therefore mean thousands of candidate checks and payload reads. `LIMIT 1` bounds returned rows, not candidates inspected; today's reported 1,403 maximum is inventory, not a ceiling.

This is an uncorrelated scalar lookup, not a jobs search per assignment row. It need only run when the released-holding branch needs its cutoff; all-open/no-matching-holding cases may avoid it. That qualification does not bound the long-context case it must handle.

The outer holding lookup also changes its access requirements. The schema has only `community_assignments_open_by_seat(seat) WHERE to_at IS NULL` and a primary key beginning with `(project,role,instance,seat,from_at)` (`migrations/0032_community_assignments.sql:23-27`). The new open-OR-released predicate cannot use that partial index to cover released holdings. There is no full seat-leading/time index for the new branch: a complete query plan must account for possible unrelated fleet-assignment traversal, not only the inner `SEARCH jobs USING INDEX jobs_serial` line. A no-sort primary-key traversal does not make that traversal seat-bounded.

`fetch_all` materializes every matching assignment before Rust converts, sorts and deduplicates it (`memory_turn.rs:414-465`). R returned historical instances cost their full row bytes plus O(R log R) sorting/string comparisons before U unique holdings survive. Neither repeated instances nor a long-lived context is capped.

**This work is outside the advertised hold bound.** Both compact and close await `turn_for` before calling `hold`; `hold` only then takes `Pending` and starts its deadline (`http/mod.rs:2533-2547`, `http/lifecycle.rs:340-360`, `memory_turn.rs:240-251`). Thus the existing five-minute deadline does not bound this new lookup/materialization/sort. A duplicate request also pays the query before the pending-turn guard rejects it. Store lock/acquisition timeouts are not a statement/history-walk deadline. No measured timeout or CPU regression is claimed; the missing limit is source-derived.

**Required:** use a directly indexed last-done-compact/checkpoint lookup rather than searching body-job history, give released holdings a genuine seat/context access path, and include potentially large pre-hold work in an explicit bounded recovery path. If that work cannot complete within its budget, preserve F130 by taking the existing generic memory turn, not by silently treating truncated history as no holdings. CI should pin the complete query plan and exercise many unrelated holdings, thousands of delivery jobs, no previous compact and budget/error recovery. The current behavior tests do not prove those properties.

**Other cost:** no new executable site or recurring poll/tick query. Compaction-wake retains the old open-holdings read. Newly covered released-role/store-error cases can add one existing memory prompt, live event subscription, admission task, deadline and report per accepted turn; the per-seat pending guard prevents duplicate accepted turns, not duplicate pre-hold reads. Prompt/model work and any memory writes the recipient performs are real additional work versus the old direct compact/close path, through existing delivery/writer sites. Released labels use the existing in-process timezone helper, once per displayed released holding; no `date` launch is added.

Verified all 14 memory-turn HTTP cases, release/done-compact/store-error regressions, prompt/dedup/local-time tests and all six spawn guards. Rust lint, Node22/24 and delivers checks succeed. Existing admission/wait deadline tests do not cover the pre-hold database phase. The author-reported query plan/mutations were not reproduced locally.

Worktree/GitHub heads agree; clean and CLEAN. No local Cargo, tests, SQL/query-plan probe, workload, store mutation, restart or product edit. This block concerns unbounded lifecycle-entry work, not the released-role memory requirement.
